grade.name: Form 1
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 1" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

topics.name: TOPIC 1.9 TONE COLOUR (TIMBRE)
topics.description: Tone color, also known as timbre, refers to the distinct quality or character of a sound that allows us to differentiate between different voices or instruments playing the same pitch and loudness. It helps musicians express emotion, style, contrast, and texture, as well as identify and blend voices and instruments in an ensemble.

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC 1.9.1 VOCAL TIMBRES
sub_topics.description: Refers to the unique qualities of a singer's voice shaped by vocal cord structure, vocal tract resonance, and singing techniques.

competencies.description: Contrast female from male vocal timbres

sub_topics.name: SUB TOPIC: 1.9.2 INSTRUMENTAL TIMBRE
sub_topics.description: Examines how instrumental timbre creates texture, mood, and emotion, adding richness and diversity to musical compositions.

competencies.description: Identify tone qualities of indigenous and western musical instruments

topics.name: TOPIC 1.10: VOICE
topics.description: Refers to the human singing voice as an instrument that produces pitches, rhythms, melodies, and lyrics using the vocal cords, mouth, and respiratory system. Understanding the voice enables effective and confident singing.

sub_topics.name: SUB TOPIC 1.10.1 PRINCIPLES OF SINGING
sub_topics.description: Covers fundamental concepts guiding proper vocal techniques (such as breath control, posture, articulation, diction, and projection) to produce healthy and expressive sound.

topics.name: TOPIC: 1.11 MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS:
topics.description: Devices that produce musical sounds, categorized into families by sound production methods. Learning instruments improves memory, concentration, creativity, confidence, and emotional expression.

sub_topics.name: SUBTOPIC: 1.11.1 CLASSIFICATION OFMUSICALINSTRUMENTS
sub_topics.description: Focuses on identifying African (idiophone, membranophone, chordophone, aerophone) and Western (woodwind, string, brass, percussion) instrument classes.

sub_topics.name: SUB-TOPIC: 1.11.2 HANDLING AND PLAYING MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS
sub_topics.description: Covers basic handling, sound production, hygiene, storage, and maintenance needed to preserve sound quality, playability, and longevity of instruments.

competencies.description: Apply basic principles in handling and playing of musical instruments

topics.name: TOPIC 1.12.1: MUSICAL ARTS AND TECHNOLOGY
topics.description: The application of computers, hardware, and software to compose, record, perform, and analyze music. It enhances music theory understanding, performance, and creative expression.

sub_topics.name: SUBTOPIC 1.12.1 INTRODUCTION TO MUSIC TECHNOLOGY
sub_topics.description: Focuses on identifying audio hardware (input, output, signal processors) and software (DAWs, plugins) as well as understanding their basic functions and signal paths.

competencies.description: Identify available music hardware and soft wares
